newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-WRAY GROUP WINS LANDSLIDE VOTE TO TAKE OVER FOREST.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WRAY GROUP WINS LANDSLIDE VOTE TO TAKE OVER FOREST.

text.p: A consortium led by property developer Nigel Wray was given the go-ahead to take over English premier league soccer club Nottingham Forest on Monday after an overwhelming vote in favour by shareholders.

The 19-million-pound ($30.9 million) bid from Wray's Bridgford consortium was accepted at an extraordinary general meeting by 189 votes with only seven against, according to Larry Lloyd, a former Forest player.
"I'm absolutely delighted," Lloyd, a shareholder himself, told Reuters by phone after the meeting. "It was the only choice we could make to try to save this club."
Bridgford includes Wray, chairman of property group Burford and owner of Saracens rugby union club, author Phil Soar and former Tottenham Hostpur chairman Irving Scholar.
The consortium plans to pump 16 million pounds into the club to strengthen a squad battling against relegation.
Some three million pounds will be available to shareholders who wish to take the cash and the consortium will inherit debts estimated at around seven million pounds.
The group plans to float the club and is anxious for it to maintain its premier league status. The former European champions are currently languishing third from bottom of the division.

Wray's group was the only bidder left in the battle for Forest by Monday after a consortium led by U.S. journalist Albert Scardino was forced out of the reckoning by the withdrawal of its main backer, Mercury Asset Management . ($ = 0.614 British Pounds)
